title: Ministry of Steel to hold Open House on Steel Import Issues on 21st August
body_text:
Ministry of Steel will be conducting Open House to discuss issues related to import of steel on 21 st August 2026 in Steel Room, 3rd Floor, GPOA- 3, Netaji Nagar New Delhi . Companies and associations may present their issues related to above subjects in the Open House. To participate in the Open House e-mails may be sent on tech-steel[at]nic[dot]in for getting a confirmed time slot on above date.
While sending the e-mail, following information may be included:
Name of the Company/Association Type of industry and product – Auto/Aerospace/Telecom/ Defence, etc. Issue is related to SIMS/SARAL SIMS/QCO EXEMPTION Reference of SIMS/SARAL SIMS/QCO EXEMPTION application if any Issue in brief (maximum 50 words) Name and designation of participant (third party representation not allowed) Contact details of the participant (mobile number and e-mail)
The Open House will be conducted from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM and specific time slots will be indicated via e-mail. Walk-ins will not be possible due to logistic challenges and only one representative per organisation is permitted to ensure wider participation.
It is advised that any company or association having issues related to SIMS/SARAL SIMS/QCO EXEMPTION for import of steel may send their request on the above e-mail by 18 th August 2026, 2:00 pm to get confirmed time-slots.
***
AG

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Steel will hold an Open House on 21 August 2026 at its Delhi office to address stakeholder issues related to steel import processes, specifically SIMS, SARAL SIMS, and QCO exemptions. Companies and associations must register by emailing tech-steel@nic.in by 18 August 2026, 2:00 PM, providing specified details, to receive a confirmed time slot. Walk-ins are not permitted, and only one representative per organisation may attend.
enrichment.context: SIMS (Steel Import Monitoring System) and its simplified version SARAL SIMS are registration mechanisms requiring importers to furnish advance information on steel shipments, aimed at tracking import trends and curbing dumping of low-quality or subsidised steel. Quality Control Orders (QCOs) under the BIS Act mandate that steel products meet Indian quality standards, and industries like auto, aerospace, telecom, and defence sometimes seek exemptions when domestically certified grades are unavailable. This Open House is a routine administrative/consultative mechanism for resolving procedural bottlenecks faced by industry in import compliance, rather than a new policy or scheme announcement.
